verdict.rationale: Azure's own RBAC documentation describes fine-grained access management for Azure resources. It also gives an example of scoping permissions so one user manages VMs and another manages virtual networks within a subscription, which covers the core of resource-scoped least privilege. missing for 10: evidence of conditional policies (attribute/condition-based assignments), documented policy evaluation logic (e.g., deny/allow precedence), explicit resource-level scope hierarchy detail, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, least privilege is expressible — fine-grained IAM policies with conditions, resource-level scoping, and documented policy evaluation

citations.quote: Azure RBAC is an authorization system built on Azure Resource Manager that provides fine-grained access management to Azure resources.
Allow one user to manage virtual machines in a subscription and another user to manage virtual networks
